messages.subject: multiple transition lists
messages.body_plain:
Dear MsStats Team,

I run label-free SRM experiment for 108 proteins in two conditions (wild type and mutant) with 4 biological replicates each (replicates 1-8); the 108 targets were separated in two transition lists in such a way that some peptides from the same protein were registered in two different runs. I included the same housekeeping endogenous peptides in every run so list 1 and list 2. After data analysis with MsStats 3.5.3 I noticed elevated p-values for many targets comparing to global label free proteomics results and also to previous SRM experiment run with the same conditions but limited amount of targets that comprised in one transition list. I would like to ask you how MsStats deals with two inclusion lists. I used following dataProcess function for normalization

dataProcess(raw = LCndbCDataTwoRunsList,

                                  normalization = 'globalStandards', nameStandards=c('x','y','z','r'),

                                  MBimpute=TRUE,

                                  censoredInt='0',

                                  cutoffCensored='minFeature',

                                  skylineReport = TRUE)

and following command for compatison

comparison<-matrix(c(1,-1), nrow=1)

row.names(comparison)<-"Mut-WT"

comparison

Mut.comparisons <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix = comparison, data=LCndbCDataTwoRunsList.TMP.wStandard)

I made the calculation with above functions for a subset of 6 proteins (3 housekeeping, 3 real targets) in two ways:

-          keeping original Run assignment where peptides were in different transition lists so Run1 and Run2

-          Changing all Run 2 to Run 1 simulating one transition list.

For two most important targets d and e the p-values are different in both calculations while the FC looks similar. I’ve also checked condition plots and in both cases the difference looks significant.

I would like to ask you if it is a problem when the MsStat’s algorithm considers two transition lists as technical replicates. Is condition plot enough to prove the significant alteration in expression?

Kind regards
Dorota

When multiple groups are compared against a control group in the external tool of Skyline, the average level of those groups will be used for the comparison as you noticed. messages.subject: dataProcess Settings for DIA Experiments
messages.body_plain:
Hi, MSstats team.

Will you please suggest optimal dataProcess settings for DIA experiments? I'm currently having difficulty determining what settings to use for the following arguments:

featureSubset
"all"(default) uses all features that the data set has. "top3" uses top 3 features which have highest average of log2(intensity) across runs. "topN" uses top N features which has highest average of log2(intensity) across runs. It needs the input for n_top_feature option. "highQuality" selects the most informative features which agree the pattern of the average features across the runs.

remove_proteins_with_interference
TRUE allows the algorithm to remove the proteins if deem interfered. FALSE (default) does not allow to remove the proteins, in which all features are interfered. In this case, the proteins, which will completely loss all features by the algorithm, will keep the most abundant peptide.

censoredInt
Missing values are censored or at random. ’NA’ (default) assumes that all ’NA’s in ’Intensity’ column are censored. ’0’ uses zero intensities as censored intensity. In this case, NA intensities are missing at random. The output from Skyline should use ’0’. Null assumes that all NA intensites are randomly missing.

cutoffCensored
Cutoff value for censoring. only with censoredInt=’NA’ or ’0’. Default is ’minFeature’, which uses minimum value for each feature.’minFeatureNRun’ uses the smallest between minimum value of corresponding feature and minimum value of corresponding run. ’minRun’ uses minumum value for each run.

MBimpute
only for summaryMethod="TMP" and censoredInt=’NA’ or ’0’. TRUE (default) imputes ’NA’ or ’0’ (depending on censoredInt option) by Accelated failure model. FALSE uses the values assigned by cutoffCensored.

Thanks in advanced.

Scott

messages.subject: Re: multiple transition lists
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dorota,

Thank you for pointing out the issue from multiple injection (different transition lists in separate injection for one sample).

1. We recommend not to merge two runs before normalization. need to keep separate runs.

2. We realized that there is the issue for summarization level in case of multiple injections. As you mentioned, it recognized as technical replicates. We will fix it.

3. Condition plot is just for descriptive purpose. So, Actually, not the same as significance. For data visualization and checking data itself, we recommend to check profile plot. In order to check significance with CI, recommend to see comparison plot from 'groupComparisonPlot'.

Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena

messages.subject: Re: Intensity has 0 or negative values
messages.body_plain:
Thank you for sharing the data Scott.

1. MSstats expects the data should have (the number of feature times the number of MS run) rows. If not, there are incomplete rows. In your case, I found that you have separate transition list, which means multiple injection with different transition lists from one sample. So, NA for other transitions, which are not measured in certain run, should be reported in data too. (For example, Run1 has the intensity for transition1,2, but not fur transition 3,4, which will be measured in Run2. Then still NAs for transition 3,4 of Run1 are needed in the dataset) But users do not worry about it. MSstats will add incomplete rows. It need to recognize the design of experiments.

2. I think that problem is multiple injection. As Dorota reported, MSstats currently recognized it as technical replicates and We will fix it soon.

Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena

messages.body_plain:
Scott,

Default is our suggested optimal setting for dataProcess. I recommend to use default for all options except 'censoredInt'.
Different spectral processing tools report differently for missing values. I recommend as below in current stage.

Skyline, Progenesis : censoredInt='0'
MaxQuant, Spsectronaut, openSWATH : censoredInt='NA'

If you use other tool, then use 'censoredInt=0' if they report zero for missing values, or use 'censoredInt=NA' if they report NA for missing values.

Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena

messages.subject: Re: Visualise the imputed data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Cheng,

You can't export or extract the imputed value. Imputed values are used to get run-level summarized value (xxx$RunlevelData) in dataProcess step. xxx$RunlevelData is used for inference step (Hypothesis testing).

imputed data is not used for any plots from dataProcessPlots ( profile plot, QC plot, condition plot).

- Meena

messages.subject: globalStandards Normalization and p/q-values
messages.body_plain:
Hi, MSstats team.

I have a question about the results of a DIA dataset that I analyzed. I used the TMP model and normalized using the globalStandards option. The global standard is Pierce PRTC peptides that were spiked into each sample. I performed a protein level analysis, but when I look at the results, the global standard "protein" doesn't have a p or q-value of 1 (it's less than 1). It's my understanding that when I normalize to global standards, the denominator ends up being the sum of the transition areas of all of the global standard peptides. Because all of the global standard peptides are in the same protein, I would expect to get p- and q-values of exactly 1. Am I misunderstanding how the global standards normalization works?

Thanks in advance.

Scott

messages.subject: Re: globalStandards Normalization and p/q-values
messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,

Normalization using the 'globalStandards' option is based on the log intensities of the selected standard peptides and/or proteins (provided in the 'nameStandards' option). It takes three steps: (a) get the mean of features for each standard (in each run), (b) get the mean among all standards (in each run), (c) equalize the mean value calculated in step (b) to the median across runs.

Note that this mean value is not used for group comparison. Instead, group comparison is based on the outputs of run-level summarization, using for example, TMP.

HTH
Tsung-Heng
